EXPOSURE - THIS IS NOT A BLIND READING (faces 1-2)
- The overview image-001 itself carries modern pencil notes in the lower margin of the right-hand page that state a proposed identification: roughly "Aeneas Silvius [Piccolomini?]", "Rede ... Reg.? in Regensburg", "1454 23/4", "(cf. ... S. 461)". The same overview has at the top "bis 1964 als Einband zur Hs 308" and the shelf note "Stams, StA, Frg. 121_1r"; image-010 has "Stams, StA, Frg. 121_1v" and a pencil note in the left margin "1455/53? (28.10.1456?)"; image-019 "...Frg. 121_2r"; image-028 "bis 1964 im Einband zu Hs 308", "...Frg. 121_2v". I saw the identification note before reading the text of faces 1-2. I did not consult any edition or my memory of one, and I transcribed only what I see, but readers of this response should treat faces 1-2 as exposed. No identification is written on faces 3-4 (images 019, 028) as far as I can see.
- My standing context also contained a project note mentioning a "Stams pilot" for a manuscript-fragment identification project (no work named). 
- Beyond the rules: I listed the packet directory to get filenames. Nothing else opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Four overviews: image-001 (face 1; tiles 002-005 left page, 006-009 right page), image-010 (face 2; 011-014 left, 015-018 right), image-019 (face 3; 020-023 left, 024-027 right), image-028 (face 4; 029-032 left, 033-036 right). Each overview shows an opened bifolium of paper, two pages side by side, single column per page, c. 40-48 lines per page. Heavy damage: torn upper and lower edges, holes along the fold, stains, fading (especially face 2 and the right page of face 4, also a large faded/abraded zone on the right page of face 2).
- Script: one hand, small cursive/hybrid gothic in brown ink; no colour visible. Few abbreviations beyond standard suspensions (p-bar, q(ue), (christ)i-, d(omi)n(u)s, -(us), -(um)).
- Faces 1-2: continuous prose with no headings; some words underlined in the same or a later ink (e.g. "anno proximo in germanos", "turcos aut tartaros", "Hunyat? Comes", "Germanie"); a few interlinear corrections/insertions and one left-margin note (image-003 l.12) and one right-margin note (image-012 l.7).
- Faces 3-4: prose divided by headings written in a larger, darker display script, outdented into the left margin or set within the line: "Ethimologia" (image-020), "Super(est)? ..." (image-024), "Concathenate sunt inter se discipline" (image-026), "Auctoritas" (enlarged initial, image-023), "Locuturo aut(em) michi de poetis eorumque lectionibus..." (image-027), "Barbarismus quidem" (image-033/034), "Soloecismum" (image-035), "Racionemque reddi de gramatica" (image-036). Show-through of text from the other side is visible at the right edge of face 4 (mirror letters), and at the top of image-033.
- Tentative interpretation: faces 1-2 are a single oration/exhortation (addressing princes and "germani" about war against the Turks); faces 3-4 are a grammatical/rhetorical treatise (etymology, consuetudo, barbarism, solecism, reading of poets). No main-text/commentary layout.

CONVENTIONS
- Line numbers are counted from the top of each tile, including a partial first line if visible. Tiles overlap by 2-4 lines; where a line repeats from the previous tile I start numbering the new text after the overlap and say so. I have not transcribed every line; selected spans are listed per page.
- ( ) = expansion; ? after a word = uncertain reading; [illegible] or "..." inside a line = letters seen but not read; [ ] = notes.
